title: Reaching 75%: Reforming Singapore's Public Transport System
what_it_is: Reaching 75%: Reforming Singapore's Public Transport System

sections.label: Public transport peak hour target
sections.summary: LTA aims for 75% of peak hour journeys by public transport by 2030, but as of financial year 2024 it is 66%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To begin with, the LTA aims to have 75% of all peak hour journeys carried out via public transport by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As of financial year 2024, it is a mere 66%, and with just four years to go, I wonder if this target will soon be quietly revised.

sections.label: Local bus captains and subsidies
sections.summary: Local bus captains fell from 54% to 41% between 2021 and 2025, while public transport subsidies exceed $2 billion yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: From 2021 to 2025, the proportion of local bus captains dropped from 54% to 41%, with two local bus captains leaving the industry for every new local hire.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Ramping up public transport capacity presumably comes at a cost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And as the Government often reiterates, our public transport services are heavily subsidised by the Government, with former Transport Minister S Iswaran stating in 2022 that this stands at more than $2 billion per year and this includes a subsidy of around $1 billion for trains and another $1 billion for buses.

sections.label: Rail financing models compared
sections.summary: SMRT's lines moved to NRFF version two in 2016, while the Thomson-East Coast Line and Jurong Region Line use a service fee model.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In 2016, a decade ago, the LTA bought over $1.06 billion of operating assets from SMRT and moved its lines onto NRFF version two, which introduced fare revenue shortfall sharing and an earnings before interest and taxes' cap and collar that effectively caps the operator's margin at around 5%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, the Thomson-East Coast Line was awarded to SMRT in 2017 via a limited tender on an entirely different basis: a service fee model where the Government collects all fare revenue, bears all fare revenue risk and pays the operator a fee of about $1.7 billion over nine years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Jurong Region Line, awarded in November 2024 to a joint venture between SBS Transit Rail and RATP Dev for approximately $750 million over up to 11 years, is on the same service fee model.

sections.label: Call for renewed rail framework
sections.summary: A decade after SMRT's privatisation and NRFF version two, the speaker calls for a unified service-fee framework and a single publicly owned rail operator.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It has been a decade since SMRT was privatised, and NRFF version two was rolled out in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I therefore call for a renewed rail financing framework: to complete the convergence of all rail lines onto a single, unified service-fee framework, and go one step further by consolidating rail operations under a single, publicly owned national rail operator.

sections.label: Rail Reliability Taskforce recommendations
sections.summary: The Rail Reliability Taskforce, formed September 2025 and chaired by the LTA Chief Executive, recommended accelerated renewal, spare parts management and standardised condition-monitoring.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Rail Reliability Taskforce formed in September 2025 is chaired by the LTA Chief Executive and comprises the Group CEOs of both SMRT and SBS Transit, precisely because rail reliability cannot be managed operator by operator.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Its recommendations, which the Ministry accepted in February this year, call for accelerated renewal of trains, signalling and power systems, better management of spare parts, and more comprehensive, standardised condition‑monitoring across the rail network.

sections.label: Commit to unified service-fee model
sections.summary: The speaker calls for committing to a renewed rail financing framework converging all lines onto a single service-fee model under one licence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, commit to a renewed rail financing framework that converges all existing lines onto a single, unified service-fee model under one licence, ahead of the Cross Island Line's opening in 2030 and upon the gradual expiry of existing licences.

sections.label: AV roll-out and autonomous buses
sections.summary: AV roll-out remains largely in trial phase with about 20 AVs in Punggol and six autonomous buses due on Bus Services 400 and 191 in second half of 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Yet, over a decade later, our AV roll-out remains largely in the trial phase, with only around 20 AVs involved in short, fixed route services in Punggol.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We also have six autonomous buses procured at a contract value of $8 million, due to start operating on Bus Services 400 and 191 in the second half of 2026.

sections.label: Bus captain nationality and shortages
sections.summary: As of December 2024 only 28% of public bus captains are Singaporeans, 57% are foreign work pass holders, and 42 school bus operators may recruit more foreign drivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: That concern is legitimate and deserves to be taken seriously.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, even as the demand for public bus captains has grown, as of December 2024 only 28% are Singaporeans, with 57% foreign work pass holders required to supplement the driver pool.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In fact, 42 school bus operators have been allowed to recruit more foreign drivers than under the standard provision to alleviate an acute shortage of drivers.

sections.label: Transport research investment and mode share
sections.summary: MOT plans to invest $800 million over five years on transport research and innovation, while public transport mode share rose from 62% to 66% in eight years against a 75% target.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Minister for Transport shared during the debate on the Transport Motion that "MOT plans to invest $800 million over the next five years on transport research and innovation to support efforts to develop frontier technology".

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To conclude, Mr Speaker, our public transport mode share has crawled from 62% to 66% in eight years, against a 75% target that is now four years away.

sections.label: Public transport spending and mode share
sections.summary: The 75% peak-period mode share ambition is reflected in about $2 billion a year spent on public transport operating costs, plus larger sums for infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Our ambition to achieve 75% peak-period mode share reflects this.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We invest heavily in our public transport system, about $2 billion a year on public transport operating costs, on top of much larger sums for infrastructure.

sections.label: Rail network expansion
sections.summary: The rail network is growing from 275 kilometres today to about 360 kilometres by the early 2030s with the Jurong Region Line and Cross Island Line.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We know that once commuters are on the rail network, most journeys are fast and reliable.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: This is why we are growing the rail network from 275 kilometres today to about 360 kilometres by the early 2030s, with the opening of the Jurong Region Line and Cross Island Line.

sections.label: Bus package tendering service fees
sections.summary: Since transiting to tendering out bus packages, service fees paid by the Government to operators have dropped by 15%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Since we transited to tendering out bus packages, service fees paid by the Government to the operators have dropped by 15%.

sections.label: NRFF consolidated rail asset ownership
sections.summary: The NRFF consolidated asset ownership under the Government, enabling a long-term view of asset renewal, common standards and coordinated rail investments.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The NRFF consolidated asset ownership under the Government, which enabled us to take a long-term view of asset renewal, drive common standards and to coordinate investments across the rail network.

sections.label: Rail reliability and operator capabilities
sections.summary: The test is whether the network delivers good service, and high rail reliability standards above the one million mean kilometres between failure target have been achieved.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Ultimately, the question is not what industry model we have but rather, the test is whether we are able to operate our network to deliver good service.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We have achieved and maintained high rail reliability standards, above our one million mean kilometres between failure target.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Our operators have grown their capabilities to manage an expanding network, to provide faster journeys and better connectivity over time.

sections.label: Planning, investments and Sitting time
sections.summary: Sound planning and sustained investments are needed, and the Sitting tomorrow will commence at 10.30 am under Standing Order 2(3)(a).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We need both sound planning and sustained investments, supported by the right structures and operating models.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We will continue to improve journey times and connectivity, while ensuring that our public transport system remains well-run and financially sustainable so that public transport is the travel mode of choice for most Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Pursuant to Standing Order 2(3)(a), I wish to inform hon Members that the Sitting tomorrow will commence at 10.30 am.
